question: Should OpenClaw allow sandboxed sessions to request ACP host or worker spawns, and which security boundary should own that capability?
rationale: The code can implement a host bridge, sidecar, or isolated worker path, but automation should not choose whether sandboxed sessions may cross into host-side ACP execution or what trust model makes that acceptable.

options.title: Prefer Isolated ACP Workers
options.body: Extend the execution-backend/profile design so ACP runs in sandboxed workers or sidecars with explicit auth, workspace, secret, lifecycle, and audit boundaries before enabling sandboxed requesters.

options.title: Approve Audited Host Bridge
options.body: Add an opt-in host-side ACP proxy with narrow spawn/steer/cancel APIs, allowlists, rate limits, durable audit logs, and operator warnings for controlled privilege escalation.

options.title: Keep The Current Block
options.body: Continue documenting that sandboxed sessions must use runtime="subagent" or run ACP-capable harnesses inside the container until a stronger design is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Prefer Isolated ACP Workers
recommendation.body: Extend the execution-backend/profile design so ACP runs in sandboxed workers or sidecars with explicit auth, workspace, secret, lifecycle, and audit boundaries before enabling sandboxed requesters.
